items.title: Cascadu interviewed by Monk Rowe, Clinton, New York, November 15, 2019
items.q: these photos we are looking at taken by Milt Hinton

ctx.x: picked up, they got their chops on the street. They got their chops on the stage. They got their chops, you know, on the road you know? And it became something that they lived. It became something that gave them — that fed their spirit. Their body might have deteriorated but their spirit and their soul was being fed by something that we can’t put our finger on.

Exactly. And I have experienced that with people like, these photos we are looking at taken by Milt Hinton and that generation, somehow in talking to them and just sitting next to them you felt better afterwards, like they were passing on whatever it is that we can’t nail down, but it is something that gets passed on.

And they live it. We live it. And I’m fortunate, I feel really really blessed at this stage in my life to be doing something like what we did yesterday in the performance and performing with other people etcetera, and being able to touch lives. You know I remember, you know, in Trinidad we had, part of the carnival culture was to have these huge brass bands on the road. And I had belonged to one of the big and really hot brass bands back in the 80s into the early 90s in Trinidad. And it shaped the lives of so…
